title: Spinor condensate persistent currents in an atomtronic Josephson necklace
authors: Sayan Chatterjee, Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract: The investigation of superflow in multi-junction Josephson circuits is currently a leading frontier of physics research, probing the fundamental manifestations of macroscopic phase coherence and enabling applications to quantum simulation, metrology and computing. In this work, we extensively investigate the stability and dynamics of persistent currents of a spinor atomic Bose-Einstein condensate on a ring with multiple Josephson junctions. Specifically, we examine the effects of positive and negative interspecies interactions, co- and counter-rotation, population and Manakov asymmetry, as well as Rabi coupling on the persistent currents carried by the two components. Our analysis reveals that the presence of a second species offers multiple mechanisms for unprecedented manipulation of supercurrents on the ring, including phase-slip engineering, stability control, current-inversion switching and supercurrent pumping. Our study provides a roadmap for the engineering of persistent currents in binary ring condensates in necklace potentials, with significant implications for atomtronics, matter-wave interferometry and sensing using atomic Bose gases.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how persistent supercurrents in spinor Bose-Einstein condensates can be controlled using engineered Josephson junctions. By analyzing the role of interspecies interactions (g_12), the authors show that these interactions stabilize the supercurrent against decay, even in higher dimensions. This work offers a powerful toolset for designing next-generation atomtronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the stability and dynamics of persistent supercurrents in spinor atomic Bose-Einstein condensates confined to a ring structure with multiple Josephson junctions.
main_result: The presence of a second atomic species allows for unprecedented control over supercurrents, enabling mechanisms like phase-slip engineering and current-inversion switching.
method: The research employs numerical simulations solving coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations (GPE) in both 1D ring and 2D toroidal geometries.
model_or_system: The system is a binary spinor BEC, modeled by coupled GPEs, simulating superflow in an 'atomtronic Josephson necklace' potential. The model incorporates intra- and inter-species interactions, Rabi coupling, and external barriers.
key_observables: Persistent current (winding number, L_p), current stability lifetime (τ_1), local superfluid velocity (v_local), and density profiles.
important_parameters: Interspecies interaction ratio (g_12), Rabi coupling strength (Omega), barrier height (V_0), and temperature (T).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares zero-temperature GPE results with finite-temperature sGPE results, and extends the findings from 1D to 2D toroidal geometries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate current decay versus stabilization as g_12 increases (Fig. 1, 2), show the dependence of stability on parameters in phase diagrams (Fig. 2c, Fig. 4), and demonstrate vortex nucleation vs. stable circulation in 2D (Fig. 6).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system by first establishing the 1D model, demonstrating how increasing interspecies interaction (g_12) stabilizes the current against decay. It then extends this analysis to include finite temperature effects (sGPE) and finally generalizes the findings to a 2D toroidal geometry, confirming the robustness of the stabilization mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical roadmap for controlling macroscopic quantum phenomena (supercurrents) in engineered atomic systems, directly relevant to developing quantum simulators and novel quantum devices using ultracold atoms.
